AP-1 Cellular Memory: Kinase Analysis

Reproducible analysis of persistent kinase expression and interference responses

1 Overview

This report documents a reproducible computational analysis of kinase expression associated with cellular memory in the AP-1 cellular adaptation model.

The analysis is based on the study:

Li J, Ravindran PT, O’Farrell A, et al. AP-1 mediates cellular adaptation and memory formation. Nature Communications 17, 4265 (2026).

The goal of this downstream analysis is to identify kinase genes associated with the post-dexamethasone memory state and examine how those kinase responses behave under AP-1-related interference conditions.

2 Reproducible workflow

The complete workflow is executed with:

Rscript run_all.R

The main analysis pipeline is:

00_fetch_data.R
        ↓
01_setup_and_data.R
        ↓
02_initial_Dex_response.R
        ↓
03_persistent_kinase_memory.R
        ↓
04_kinase_interference.R
        ↓
05_integrated_kinase_trajectory.R
        ↓
06_make_final_kinase_figure.R

The workflow automatically retrieves the required public input files when the data/ directory is missing.

3 Input data

The analysis uses:

data/log2CPM_matrix.txt
data/studydesign.tsv
data/dex_log2FC.txt
data/dextable.txt
data/KinHubKinaseList.csv

The AP-1 RNA-seq files originate from the public cellular-memory repository:

https://github.com/arjunrajlaboratory/cellularmemory

Relevant source directory:

extractedData/burninrnaseq/202208/

The kinase reference list is obtained from the KinHub/OpenKinome resource.

4 Load analysis outputs

5 Data integrity and sample alignment

The expression dataset contains 191 analyzable samples after alignment with the experimental design.

Sample_147 is present in the design metadata but is absent from the final expression matrix and is therefore excluded during the alignment step.

The setup script verifies that the final metadata order exactly matches the expression-matrix sample order before downstream analysis.

13 Reproducibility

The repository uses renv to record the R package environment.

A fresh clone can be reproduced with:

git clone <repository-url>
cd AP1_cellular_memory_analysis

Restore the package environment:

Rscript -e "renv::restore()"

Then execute the complete workflow:

Rscript run_all.R

The data-fetching script automatically downloads the required external data when they are not already present.

15 Summary

This reproducible workflow:

  1. retrieves the required public datasets;
  2. validates sample alignment;
  3. quantifies the initial dexamethasone kinase response;
  4. identifies persistent kinase-associated memory;
  5. evaluates JNK-IN-8 and T-5224 interference conditions;
  6. integrates kinase trajectories;
  7. generates the final kinase trajectory figure.

The current analysis identifies nine kinase candidates that pass the defined memory-associated kinase FDR criterion.

Their initial-response, memory, and interference profiles are retained in the integrated result table for downstream biological interpretation.

16 ATAC-seq integration of the nine kinase candidates

An additional chromatin-accessibility analysis was performed for the nine FDR-significant memory-associated kinase candidates using the processed ATAC-seq data from the original AP-1 cellular-memory study.

Gene-body plus 2 kb upstream bigWig accessibility was summarized across:

  • 3-day DMSO;
  • 3-day Dex;
  • Dex followed by DMSO;
  • DMSO followed by trametinib;
  • Dex followed by trametinib.

These regional bigWig summaries are used as descriptive accessibility trajectories and are not treated as formal differential-accessibility tests.

For formal peak-level evidence, the authors’ DESeq2 differential ATAC results for Dex-to-Tram versus DMSO-to-Tram were intersected with the nine kinase regions.

Peak-level ATAC evidence for the nine memory-associated kinase candidates

SNRK -0.9089 0.0220 0 0 NA NA NA No_FDR05_memory_ATAC_peak

PIM1 0.9570 0.0037 0 0 NA NA NA No_FDR05_memory_ATAC_peak
CDK2 -0.8808 0.0226 2 1 chr12:56358987-56360175 1.028 0.0035 Significant_ATAC_discordant_with_RNA
ERBB3 -1.5175 0.0096 1 0 NA NA NA No_FDR05_memory_ATAC_peak
TRIB3 0.9442 0.0065 1 0 NA NA NA No_FDR05_memory_ATAC_peak

Across the nine kinase candidates, six reported differential ATAC peaks overlapped five kinase loci. Only one overlapping peak passed FDR < 0.05.

The significant peak was associated with CDK2:

chr12:56358987-56360175
DESeq2 log2FoldChange = +1.028
adjusted P value = 0.00349

CDK2 RNA expression in the memory contrast was significantly decreased (logFC approximately -0.881; FDR approximately 0.0226), whereas accessibility at this local ATAC peak increased. Thus, the RNA and chromatin-accessibility responses are discordant.

The CDK2 peak was not represented among the peaks reported in the authors’ 3-day Dex versus DMSO differential ATAC table. It is therefore interpreted here as a memory-associated / Dex-history-associated accessibility change rather than as a canonical acute-Dex-induced learned peak.

16.1 CDK2 significant ATAC peak trajectory

Figure. Accessibility trajectory at the statistically significant CDK2 memory-associated ATAC peak. Open circles represent biological replicates and filled points represent condition means. The DESeq2 statistic refers specifically to the Dex-to-Tram versus DMSO-to-Tram comparison.

17 IGV views for the nine kinase candidates

To complement the gene-body accessibility summaries, IGV snapshots were generated for each of the nine kinase candidate loci using the ATAC-seq bigWig tracks across the relevant conditions. These panels provide visual locus-level context and help assess whether accessibility changes arise from discrete local peaks rather than only from whole-gene averaged signal.
